summary: Stevens County, WA lookout: a 45-foot L-6 pole tower built 1933 or 1934, staffed into the early 1950s, fell in 1959; ruins reported on the ground.

facts.design: 45-foot pole tower with an L-6 cab
facts.status_note: The tower fell (WillhiteWeb says blew down) in 1959; the Former Fire Lookout Sites register says it was removed in the 1950s. A local history page says ruins remain on the ground.

access.note: A trail from the official Mt. Rogers trailhead, reached by Kolle Creek Road (FR 500), climbs to the highest point. No tower remains to visit.

visit.trail_note: Drive Aladdin Road to Kolle Creek Road (FR 500) to the Mt. Rogers trailhead, where the road now ends, then walk the trail to the highest point.

events.note: A USGS survey party noted Forest Service road work and found no structure during its visit
A May 1934 Colville Examiner item reports a lookout being established; WillhiteWeb gives 1934 for the 45-foot pole tower. The register and FireLookout.com give 1933.
Mr. and Mrs. Hazen Walston listed as lookouts
A couple is listed each year from 1950 to 1954; a 1959 newspaper item says the lookout was discontinued about 1950
Last named lookouts in the sources: Mr. and Mrs. Robert Dewey
The tower fell or blew down on a Sunday night in October 1959 per the Statesman Examiner; FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb also date the fall to 1959

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com date the tower to 1933; WillhiteWeb and the Forest Lookouts page date it to 1934. A 1933 USGS visit found no structure and a May 1934 Colville Examiner item reports a lookout being established, so the story uses 1934 and notes the 1933 listings.
The register says the tower was removed in the 1950s. FireLookout.com, WillhiteWeb and a 1959 newspaper item say it fell or blew down in 1959. The story uses 1959 and notes the register's version.

A 1959 newspaper item says the lookout was discontinued about 1950, but WillhiteWeb and FireLookout.com name lookout couples through 1954. The story reports the named couples and the newspaper's claim.

notes_for_editor: Built year conflicts: 1933 (register, FireLookout.com) vs 1934 (WillhiteWeb, and a May 1934 Colville Examiner item quoted by the weebly page). The story favours 1934 because a 1933 USGS visit found no structure; the editor may prefer to show both. Fate conflicts: the register says removed in the 1950s, the other three say it fell or blew down in 1959. Staffing conflict: named couples through 1954 vs a 1959 newspaper saying discontinued about 1950. A WebSearch for a second independent source found nothing on Rogers Mountain beyond the FFLOS listing (status Gone, tower). The 1999 column cited on the weebly page is secondhand and was not checked. The 'ruins remain on the ground' claim rests on that weebly page alone. The brief's access 'unknown' was set to public from the trail description; no closure or permit was found.
